ABNORMAL RESULT

nuc ish 22q11.2(TUPLE1x3),22q13(ARSAx2)

PRELIMINARY REPORT
In situ hybridization was carried out with probe TUPLE1 (located within band 22q11.2) on interphase 
nuclei and metaphases from preparations of blood lymphocytes.

Three TUPLE 1 signals were seen in 87/110 (74%) of nuclei examined.  On metaphase chromosomes, this 
probe hybridized as expected to the proximal long arm of both homologues of chromosome 22, however 
the hybridization signal appeared larger on one homologue in the majority of cells. No hybridization
was seen elsewhere in the genome.

These results indicate that this individual has trisomy for the TUPLE1 locus, which is likely to be
due to a duplication in the proximal region of one chromosome 22 long arm. The possibility of mosaicism 
for the abnormality has not been excluded.  Further studies are in progress.

Please send blood samples in lithium heparin from both parents for inheritance studies.
